questions.coherence: One design across the font batch. Format owns the pure member rules (INPUT_LIMITS, escapes, zipMembers, slugOf/categoryOf/memberIds), session rotation (clock and start injected) and declared-credits parsing and scoping. The CLI keeps only fs reads and Date.now as thin wrappers. The editor's convertSvgLibrary composes those with importSvgBatch and importedShapePack, and registers nothing. registerSvgLibrary goes through render's registerSavedShapePacks over format's shapePackSubsetOf, the same path a saved pack takes on load, so an imported pack and a reopened one register identically. The dialog depends only on a host LibraryImporter port, so the studio (M18.17) supplies the witness, fonts, clock and registries. On the harness side, same-tree's product-tree concept now bounds its own read (pages to the base), and last-ci matches a fix by job rather than by run id, which closes both of cp26's seams. One seam remains: readZip interleaves listing and inflation, so 'refused from the central directory before any entry is inflated' holds only for the first entry (F1).

Caps from listed sizes come before any bytes() (spy-asserted). Rights, license policy and coverage are checked before any witness. Refusals are per member path. Colors are capped at 64 plus an omitted count, are exactly the lookup keys, and exclude none, currentColor and url(). A noticeFile credit is refused naming the credit, Inter carries its OFL rights, and registration is atomic with a held namespace refused. The registerSvgLibrary signature deviation is argued and the spec updated. The ZIP declared-size clause holds only for single-entry ZIPs (F1). M18.176: the dialog walks idle, converting, refused or converted, importing, imported. It refuses an incomplete declaration (no default license) before converting, re-converts only for a mapped color, and registers only the final pack. Seven component tests cover each state, plus the fieldset that is disabled while busy (r1 F1). M18.199 and M18.200 meet their EARS (see cp26DispositionsCheck). M18.195 meets its closing acceptance. M18.17 (FR-LIB-004 end to end in three browsers) is not done, as its todo state says.

findings.evidence: readZip checks the entry count up front, but then for each entry in turn it runs listingAt, the maxEntryBytes and running-total checks, and entryOrFailure, which inflates that entry before the next central-directory record is read (lines 280-290). zipMembers' doc (packages/format/src/svg-pack-members.ts:35-41) and M18.175's acceptance both state 'entry count and declared sizes refused from the central directory before any entry is inflated'. The M18.175 test (packages/editor/src/library/import-svg.test.ts:154-160) patches the declared size of a one-entry ZIP, so it cannot tell an up-front check from the interleaved one. The behaviour predates the delta (ADR-0188 era), but the delta newly claims the stronger property and puts it behind a studio picker.
findings.failure_scenario: A picked ZIP of 4096 entries whose last central-directory record declares 200 MiB inflates and CRC-checks up to 4095 earlier entries (as much as 256 MiB) before it is refused. Memory and work stay bounded by the cumulative cap, so this is no unbounded decode. But the studio's main thread does up to the full budget of inflation for an archive the listing alone could have refused, and the documented guarantee is false.
findings.recommendation: Validate all central-directory records (count, each declared size, running total, strict names) in one pass before any inflation, and add a multi-entry test whose first entry has a corrupt deflate body and whose last entry is over cap, so the size refusal must come first.
